newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weakens vs dollar amid thin supply.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weakens vs dollar amid thin supply.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened further against the dollar on Thursday on buying pressure from oil dealers amid very thin supply, commercial dealers said.
Against the dollar, Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 54.80 compared to 54.60 while against the pound, it was posted at a mean rate of 91.72 from 90.58.
"The underlying tone is that there is a lot of heavy commercial demand and supply is very thin," a dealer said.
"People are bullish about the dollar but they're finding a lot of resistance at 55 level. Spreads are as wide as 45 cents," the dealer added.
The money market was tight with overnight rates quoted as high as 23 percent.
A shift in investments from treasury bills to treasury bonds has resulted in heavy outflows of shillings from the money market, dealers said.
